newsitem.title: JAPAN: Itochu plans Vietnam truck sales company.
newsitem.headline: Itochu plans Vietnam truck sales company.

text.p: Itochu Corp said on Tuesday it soon plans to set up a joint venture company in Vietnam to sell trucks made by Isuzu Motors Ltd's Vietnamese unit.
Itochu has yet to finalise details of the joint sales company, however, an Itochu spokesman said.
Itochu is expected to form the joint venture with vehicle maintenance firm Saigon Automobile Mechanical Corp, industry sources said.

Isuzu's Vietnamese unit in Ho Chi Minh City is scheduled to start assembling two- to three-tonne Elf trucks and four-tonne trucks and buses by May, with annual output of about 1,000 vehicles, an Isuzu spokesman said.
Isuzu Vietnam previously intended to produce 2,000 vehicles per year but scaled back its plans in view of low demand in that country for expensive new trucks, he said.

Isuzu and Itochu each own 35 percent of Isuzu Vietnam. Saigon Automobile Mechanical Corp owns 26 percent, with the rest held by state-owned Govap Import-Export Co. Isuzu is 37.4 percent owned by General Motors Corp.
